reason: Premises 1–4 are directly and accurately supported by E2 and E3, which report full densification, microstructural refinement, dislocation multiplication, and quantified improvements in hardness, toughness, and oxidation onset temperature under the exact UHPS conditions proposed. Premise 5 (liquid metal corrosion resistance) is not addressed by any cited evidence, leaving a key claim unsupported.
premises: UHPS at ~15 GPa and ~1450 °C can fully densify ZrB2
UHPS induces plastic deformation, dislocation multiplication, and grain refinement in ZrB2
Grain refinement and high dislocation density enhance hardness and fracture toughness
Refined, dense microstructure raises oxidation onset temperature by ~250 °C
Dense, coherent microstructure improves resistance to liquid plating-metal corrosion
